title: Privacy-Preserving Predictive Maintenance for Industrial IoT
business: Manufacturing firms operating globally distributed factory equipment that requires predictive maintenance models.
problem: Firms cannot centralize raw sensor data due to strict data residency laws and the high bandwidth costs of transmitting massive, high-frequency vibration logs from remote factory sites to a central data center.
solution: Federated Learning enables the training of a shared predictive maintenance model by keeping raw sensor data on local factory edge servers, transmitting only model weight updates to a central aggregator.
steps: Distribute the current global model state to individual factory edge servers.
Perform local training on site-specific sensor data to compute weight updates.
Transmit only the computed weight updates back to the central server.
Aggregate the received updates using a weighted averaging method to improve the global model.
Deploy the updated global model back to all factory edge servers for inference.
outcome: A robust, globally optimized predictive maintenance model that respects regional data sovereignty while improving equipment uptime across all locations.
limitation: Communication overhead remains a constraint; monitor the frequency of synchronization rounds to ensure network stability and check for model convergence degradation.
